deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It continues Riemann's excerpt, begun on the previous page (from Erdmann's Journal für praktische Chemie, Bd. 58), of Pasteur's 1852 note in Comptes rendus 35, p. 176. The note concerns the relations between crystal form, chemical composition and rotation of the plane of polarization.

(A, continued) Pasteur claims that optically active substances generally show non-superposable ('nicht deckbare') hemihedry. He shows that apparent exceptions become hemihedral when the conditions of crystallization are changed. The page gives further examples:
- a bitartrate (written in Berzelius dot-and-bar notation as base·T̄r + Ḣ·T̄r, apparently a strontium bitartrate) crystallizes holohedrally from water and hemihedrally from another solvent;
- a sodium bitartrate is then named.
Finally, Pasteur found non-superposable hemihedry in several other optically active compounds.

(B) Compounds that differ only by opposite hemihedry, or by opposite rotation of the plane of polarization, such as dextro- and laevo-tartaric acid, behave as follows:
- combined with optically inactive compounds, they give symmetric, isomorphous products that are identical in all their other physical and chemical properties;
- combined with optically active compounds, they give products with essentially different chemical properties.
Pasteur demonstrates this with:
- the acid tartrates and active malic acid (the note adds that malic acid and aspartic acid each exist in an active and an inactive variety);
- the active alkaloids cinchonine, quinine, brucine and strychnine.

In modern terms, (B) says that enantiomers combined with an achiral partner give enantiomeric products, while combined with a chiral partner they give diastereomers with different properties. This is the basis of resolution by diastereomeric salt formation.
errors: No mathematical content to check. The chemistry is a faithful summary of Pasteur's 1852 claims. Pasteur's own generalization that every optically active substance shows hemihedral crystal faces was later found not to be universal, but that limitation belongs to Pasteur, not to a slip by Riemann.

results.what: Optically active substances crystallize with non-superposable (enantiomorphic) hemihedral faces; apparent exceptions become hemihedral when crystallization conditions are changed.
results.modern_name: Pasteur's correlation of crystal enantiomorphism (hemihedry) with optical activity

results.what: Enantiomers combined with inactive partners give compounds with identical properties; combined with active partners (e.g. cinchonine, quinine, brucine, strychnine, active malic acid) they give compounds with different properties.
results.modern_name: Enantiomer vs. diastereomer formation; basis of chiral resolution by diastereomeric salts

results.what: Malic acid and aspartic acid each exist in an active and an inactive form.
results.modern_name: Racemic vs. optically active forms (inactive aspartic and malic acids from Dessaignes' preparations)

deep.surprise_reason: These are reading notes summarizing a published Pasteur abstract. There is no original mathematics or science by Riemann; the only interest is as evidence of his reading in chemistry and crystal optics around 1852–53.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the formula is not '\sqrt[4]{R} Tr'. It appears to be a base symbol with a dot (likely Ṡr, strontium oxide) written as 'Ṡr T̄r + Ḣ T̄r', i.e. a bitartrate in Berzelius notation. 'holoedrisch 6 Wasser' is probably 'holoedrisch aus Wasser'.
Line 2: '1/8 Na Tr' is likely 'Ṅa T̄r + Ḣ T̄r' (sodium bitartrate) or 'aus N̄ ...', not a fraction.
Line 4: 'die nicht deutlichen Hemiedrie' should read 'die nicht deckbare Hemiedrie', consistent with the previous page.
In section B, 'symmetrisch isomorphe' is plausible; read 'symmetrisch isomorphe, ihren übrigen physikalischen u. chemischen Eigenschaften nach völlig gleiche Verbindungen'.

'Beweist dies nach der doppeltsauren Weinsäure' is more likely 'Beweist dies an den doppeltsauren weinsauren Salzen / an wirksamer Äpfelsäure', i.e. demonstrated with acid tartrates and active malic acid.
